findings.title: Java MessageFormat choice syntax put into an i18next bundle breaks the message
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. Every other parameterised key in this bundle (e.g. `error-invalid-length-too-short='{{0}}' must have minimal length of {{1}}.`) uses i18next double-brace interpolation, because the account console resolves these messages with i18next, not with java.text.MessageFormat. With single braces the placeholders are no longer interpolated and the `{2,choice,...}` block is not understood at all, so the end user will see the literal string `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. The change is also not needed for the sanitizer, since the old text contained no `<` character.

findings.title: Choice format in admin console i18next bundle will be rendered literally
findings.body: `error-invalid-multivalued-size` was switched from the i18next form `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to the Java MessageFormat form `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. This bundle is consumed by the admin console through i18next, which only interpolates `{{n}}` and has no support for `choice` patterns, so the admin will see the raw pattern text including `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` instead of a formatted message. Note the equivalent server-side bundle (themes/base/admin) is formatted with MessageFormat and may keep the choice form, but the keycloak.v2 bundle must not.

findings.title: Diff-trimming can compute an invalid substring range and throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: The common-prefix (`start`) and common-suffix (`end`) counters are computed independently, so for values where the removed fragment shares a prefix with the following text (or a suffix with the preceding text) `start + end` can exceed the length of `sanitized`, and `sanitized.substring(start, sanitized.length() - end)` is called with begin > end. Concrete example: English contains `<b>`, translation value is `x<div><b>y`; the sanitizer returns `x<b>y`, giving start=2 and end=4 while `sanitized.length()` is 5, so `sanitized.substring(2, 1)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. Instead of reporting the offending key, the build then aborts with an unrelated stack trace. The indices need to be clamped (e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start)`).

findings.title: Missing English source bundle aborts the build with a raw RuntimeException
findings.body: The English counterpart path is derived purely by string replacement (`resources-community` -> `resources`, locale suffix -> `_en`). If no such file exists (a theme that only lives in the community resources, a message directory without an English bundle, or a bundle name without a locale suffix) `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` fails and the IOException is rethrown as a plain `RuntimeException`, killing the whole build with a stack trace instead of producing a verification message. The same applies to reading the file under verification a few lines above. Both should either be reported through the `messages` list or be wrapped in `MojoExecutionException` like the rest of `verify()`, and a missing English bundle should be handled gracefully (e.g. treat all English values as empty).

findings.title: Anchor mismatch message does not say which file or key failed
findings.body: `messages.add("Didn't find anchor tag " + matcher.group() + " in original string")` omits both the file name and the message key, unlike the HTML message produced a few lines above which includes `key` and `file`. With hundreds of bundles a maintainer cannot locate the offending translation from this output. The `key` parameter of `santizeAnchors` is accepted but never used, so the information is already available. Additionally, after reporting the mismatch the method `break`s and leaves the remaining `<a>` tags in the value, so the subsequent policy check emits a second, redundant "Illegal HTML" message for the same key.

findings.title: HTML detection in the English source only recognises lower-case tags
findings.body:
`HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` is case sensitive, so an English source value written with an upper-case tag (e.g. `` or `
`) is classified as containing no HTML. The translation is then verified with `POLICY_NO_HTML` and every markup element it legitimately mirrors from the source is reported as "Illegal HTML", producing a false build failure that a translator cannot fix without changing the English source. Use `Pattern.CASE_INSENSITIVE` (or normalise before matching).

findings.title: Unescaping the raw value turns escaped entities into markup and can cause false positives
findings.body: `normalizeValue` runs `StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4(value)` on the raw property value before sanitizing. A translation that correctly escapes markup, e.g. `<div>`, is thereby converted into real `<div>` markup, removed by the policy, and reported as "Illegal HTML" even though the stored value is safe. The unescape step is only needed on the sanitizer output (to undo the sanitizer's own escaping); applying it to the input changes the semantics of the value being checked.

findings.title: No test asserts that a compliant bundle produces zero findings
findings.body: All four tests only use `Matchers.hasItem(...)`, so any additional (false-positive) message is silently ignored, and there is no test at all that runs `verify()` on a well-formed translation and asserts the returned list is empty. The newly added fixtures `noHtml_en.properties` and `changedAnchor_en.properties` are only used as English sources. Without a happy-path test, the many heuristics in the new code (identical anchors allowed, `{n,choice,...}` normalisation, `<!-- -->` stripping, entity unescaping, `br/p/strong/b` whitelist) can regress into false failures across hundreds of bundles without any test detecting it.

findings.title: Italian text introduced into the Lithuanian account bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users will see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. The surrounding keys (`totpStep2`, `totpStep3`) are in Lithuanian, so the intended replacement text should be a Lithuanian equivalent of "Install one of the following applications on your mobile".

findings.title: Italian text introduced into the Lithuanian login bundle
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:`, which is Italian while the rest of this file (and the following `loginTotpStep2`/`loginTotpStep3`) is Lithuanian. Lithuanian users configuring OTP at login will see an Italian instruction line.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text added to the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese wording/characters (手機, 應用程式), whereas this file is the zh_CN (Simplified) bundle and neighbouring entries use Simplified forms (e.g. `totpStep2=打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码`). The Simplified equivalent (e.g. 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：) should be used instead.
